metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.candidate_universe_and_selection_rule: Selection rule fixed before collection: examine (1) the official Swift Forums at swift.org/community as the canonical official discussion channel (language-neutral criterion: every assigned language's official/primary community hub is checked identically), (2) Stack Overflow 'swift' tag and historical Stack Overflow Trends/Developer Survey data as the largest general-purpose public Q&A source, (3) Apple Developer Forums 'Swift' tag as the vendor-run official Q&A channel, (4) the top independently-documented third-party tutorial/book ecosystem for the language (identified via search rather than picked by the benchmark), and (5) StackShare's per-language discussion/follower counts, used only as one proxy among several, never standalone.

findings.citation_support: The Swift forums are the official discussion channel for the Swift community and the best place to connect with other Swift developers (swift.org/community); forum migrated from mailing lists with dedicated subcategories for Compiler, Standard Library, Core Libraries, Package Manager, LLDB, Server, etc.
findings.claim: Official Swift Forums exist and are positioned as the primary community discussion channel, spanning Evolution, Development, Using Swift, and other categories.

findings.citation_support: The Swift community is growing and Swift Forums are growing with it; the number of projects in the Swift ecosystem keeps expanding.
findings.claim: Community and ecosystem-project discussion volume on the official forums has grown over time, with a dedicated 'Related Projects' category added to accommodate ecosystem growth, and recurring community events (e.g., Embedded Swift Community Hour).

Apple's official developer forums maintain an active, current 'Swift' tag with recent (multi-day-old) technical Q&A threads, indicating an actively used vendor-run public knowledge channel distinct from the community-run forums.

Swift won first place for 'Most Loved Programming Language' in a Stack Overflow Developer Survey, indicating strong historical public sentiment and engagement on the largest general Q&A site's own survey instrument.

Among the 500 largest Stack Overflow tags, the 'swift3' tag was noted as one of the fastest-growing tags in the year following TensorFlow's introduction, evidencing very high public Q&A volume/growth for Swift historically on the dominant programming Q&A platform. Secondary sourcing places Swift's 'Most Loved' Stack Overflow Developer Survey win in 2015 and second place in 2016.
findings.source: Stack Overflow Blog (Stack Overflow Trends, 2017) / secondary sourcing (tms-outsource.com)

findings.claim: Swift shows sustained cross-platform community engagement on a third-party technology-stack discussion site: 21.9k stacks, 17 discussion threads, and 13.6k followers.
findings.limitation: StackShare stack/follower counts are a raw popularity proxy and are not used standalone; they corroborate but do not independently establish the score.

findings.claim: Swift has an unusually large independent third-party learning-content ecosystem: Kodeco offers extensive free content plus books and high-quality tutorials, and Hacking with Swift's author is described as one of the most prolific iOS educators, continuously publishing and updating a library of books; additional community-run resources include the Try Swift conference series and Swift by Sundell.
findings.source: Kodeco (formerly Ray Wenderlich) and Hacking with Swift (via gallaugher.medium.com secondary listing)

findings.claim: Community members consistently point newcomers toward a converging, well-known set of free/paid learning resources (Hacking with Swift's 100 Days of SwiftUI, Swift by Sundell, Kodeco/raywenderlich.com, Apple's own SwiftUI tutorials), indicating a mature, well-known public knowledge base rather than fragmented or scarce resources.

limitations_and_caveats: Swift's public knowledge base is more concentrated around Apple-platform (iOS/macOS) use cases than general-purpose programming discourse, so breadth outside that domain (e.g., server-side/embedded Swift) is comparatively thinner, though growing (per Embedded Swift Community Hour activity).
Raw counts (StackShare followers, historical SO tag growth) are proxies with known limitations per methodology and are corroborating evidence only, not the sole basis for the score.

Some evidence (e.g., exact current Stack Overflow 'swift' tag question count) could not be retrieved as a precise current figure within the search budget; qualitative/comparative indicators (tag growth trends, survey placement) were used instead and are flagged as such.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.methodology_note: Predeclared sampling per Ecosystem spec: evidence collected via a fixed, deterministic route across (a) official language forum/discussion channel, (b) largest general-purpose public Q&A site (Stack Overflow) tag/topic presence, (c) vendor/official developer forum presence, (d) independent third-party learning-content ecosystem (books/tutorials/courses), and (e) one cross-language popularity-proxy site (StackShare) for consistency across the assigned language set. Same retrieval depth (2 web searches then 1 targeted follow-up) applied as for other languages in this shard batch.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.raw_score_rationale: Swift scores high (85/100) reflecting: (a) a mature, official, well-structured community forum; (b) a second, actively used vendor (Apple) Q&A channel; (c) a historically very large and fast-growing Stack Overflow presence plus a top developer-sentiment survey result; and (d) an unusually deep, independently corroborated third-party tutorial/book/course ecosystem. It is not scored at the very top of the range because its public knowledge base is more platform-concentrated (Apple ecosystem) than the most universally-discussed general-purpose languages, and because some precise current-volume figures (exact live SO tag count) were not obtainable within the retrieval budget, so qualitative/trend evidence was relied upon for part of the assessment.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.retrieval_route: Web search via provider-brokered search tool, 3 total queries executed for this metric: (1) 'Swift programming language Stack Overflow questions tag count', (2) 'Swift Forums swift.org community discussion activity', (3) 'Hacking with Swift raywenderlich Kodeco Swift tutorials number of readers'. Snapshot time: 2026-09-22 (session date).
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.scale: 0-100, 100=best; rubric-based low score used when evidence intentionally absent, not N/A
strengths: Dedicated official language forum (swift.org) with structured categories and active proposal/evolution discussion, distinct from and complementary to a large vendor forum (Apple Developer Forums).
Large historical Stack Overflow footprint with a documented top-tier growth/sentiment record (fastest-growing tag cohort in 2016-17; 'Most Loved Language' win).

Unusually rich independent tutorial/book/course ecosystem (Kodeco, Hacking with Swift, Swift by Sundell, Try Swift conferences) that is repeatedly and independently recommended across multiple unrelated sources, indicating durable, non-fragmented public knowledge availability.
Official interactive Apple tutorials (SwiftUI/DocC-based) supplement community content with vendor-maintained public learning material.
